title: Small ringed action site for a site automorphism and its exact orbit induction
statement:
Fix compatible universes and a small site $(C,J)$ with pullbacks [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $s:C\to C$ be a site automorphism, with a chosen inverse, preserving coverings and pullbacks. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings and choose a ring isomorphism $s^{-1}R\simeq R$. Write $\sigma=s^*$ for the resulting autoequivalence of $R$-module sheaves. Let $\mathcal B$ be the category of pairs $(M,\theta:\sigma M\xrightarrow{\sim}M)$ and intertwining morphisms [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

There is a small ringed site $(C\rtimes\mathbf Z,R_{\rtimes})$ whose module category is additively equivalent to $\mathcal B$. More explicitly its objects are those of $C$, its arrows $U\to V$ are pairs $(n,f:U\to s^nV)$, and $(m,h:V\to s^mW)\circ(n,f)=(n+m,s^n(h)\circ f)$. Its topology is generated by the degree-zero copies of the coverings of $C$. The sheaf $R_{\rtimes}$ restricts to $R$ and uses the coherent iterates of the chosen ring isomorphism on the other arrows. Restricting a module sheaf to the degree-zero arrows is the underlying-module functor $U:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ under the equivalence.

The same construction for sheaves of sets presents the category of sheaves equipped with an invertible $s^{-1}$-action as a sheaf topos. Its forgetful functor is the inverse image of a geometric morphism $u:\operatorname{Sh}(C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(C\rtimes\mathbf Z)$, and $u^{-1}R_{\rtimes}\simeq R$. Thus $U$ is the module pullback of a ringed-topos morphism with invertible structural ring map [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. It is exact, conservative, and creates all small limits and colimits. It also has an exact additive LEFT adjoint $\operatorname{Ind}:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$: its underlying module is $\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}\sigma^n M$, its structure isomorphism reindexes $\sigma(\bigoplus_n\sigma^n M)\simeq\bigoplus_n\sigma^{n+1}M$, and its adjunction is determined by restriction to the summand indexed by zero.

Under the site equivalence, the sheaf tensor is $M\otimes_RN$ with action $\theta_M\otimes\theta_N$ under $\sigma(M\otimes_RN)\simeq\sigma M\otimes_R\sigma N$, and the unit is $R$ with its given action. The sheaf internal Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom] restricts to $\mathcal Hom_R(M,N)$ with action given by $f\mapsto\theta_N\circ\sigma(f)\circ\theta_M^{-1}$ under $\sigma\mathcal Hom_R(M,N)\simeq\mathcal Hom_R(\sigma M,\sigma N)$. These are natural identifications on sheaves, compatible with tensor symmetry and evaluation $f\otimes x\mapsto f(x)$. No derived-category comparison is part of this assertion.

proof.text: Construct the category, topology, coefficient and the normalized module/set restriction and geometric morphism using the site-restriction theorem. It supplies no induction or closed comparisons.

Its translation functor equals sigma. Thus sigma is an equivalence; sectionwise its map preserves addition. Apply the created fixed-pair limits/colimits theorem. The module category is Grothendieck abelian by the source ringed-site theorem. Equivalence preservation and creation imply finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation, giving ModulePresentation.

Apply exact integer-orbit induction to sigma. Choose its asEquivalence as translation, which leaves all restriction data unchanged. Its sum, step, shift and zero formulas, additivity and finite exactness fill every OrbitPresentation field.
Extend the orbit presentation by its normalized tensor/Hom comparisons, retaining that presentation exactly. The resulting structure is the required Presentation.
